evidence.quote: The increases for both the three and six months ended July 31, 2026 were partially offset by lapping charges of $0.4 billion related to certain legal matters for the same periods in the previous fiscal year.

Other gains and losses for the three and six months ended July 31, 2026 consisted of net losses of $1.2 billion and $0.9 billion, respectively, compared to net gains of $2.7 billion and $2.1 billion for the same periods in the previous fiscal year.
Goodwill recorded in fiscal 2025 relates to the acquisition of VIZIO Holding Corp. in December 2024 within the Walmart U.S. segment.

supporting_evidence.quote: operating income increased $1.4 billion and $1.6 billion for the three and six months ended July 31, 2026, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous fiscal year.

input.reasoning_summary:
The initial verdict of SUPPORTED remains unchanged. The evidence clearly shows that Walmart's consolidated operating income for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was $9,383 million compared to $7,286 million for the same period in 2025, representing a $2,097 million increase (28.8% growth).

All three challenges were refuted:

H1 (One-time items): Evidence E11 shows that the Q2 2026 period actually benefited from lapping $0.4 billion in legal charges from the prior year, meaning the prior year had unfavorable one-time items that made the comparison MORE favorable, not less. Additionally, "Other gains and losses" were net losses in 2026 versus net gains in 2025, meaning non-operating items worked against the operating income comparison, not in favor of it.

H2 (Acquisitions impact): Evidence E13 indicates the VIZIO acquisition occurred in December 2024 (fiscal 2025), which would have affected both comparison periods similarly by Q2 FY2027. No evidence suggests acquisitions or divestitures materially distorted the Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025 operating income comparison.

H3 (Segment declines): Evidence E16, E17, and E18 show that all three major segments had operating income increases: Walmart U.S. (consolidated figures), Sam's Club U.S. ($485M vs $314M), and Walmart International ($1,439M vs $1,234M). There were no significant segment declines masked by the consolidated increase.

The evidence review confirms that E7 and E8 are VALID evidence with EXACT_MATCH period compatibility and ENTAILS relation to the claim.
